subject: psychology
topic: The marshmallow test did not predict what you were told
angle: The marshmallow test is linked to later success primarily because it reflects a child's early environment and social support rather than just individual self-control.
title: The Marshmallow Test Reality

hooks.text: Is your willpower actually your own?
You were told it was willpower. It is actually your environment.
You are blaming your character for your circumstances.
A child sits alone with a single white marshmallow.
The correlation drops by two thirds.

reveal.headline: Family background explains the marshmallow test.
reveal.body: The link between waiting for a marshmallow and later success is largely a reflection of a child's early environment and social support.,

explain.headline: Context matters more than willpower.
explain.body: When researchers account for family background and home environment, the correlation between waiting and achievement drops by two thirds. Trust in the person offering the reward also predicts behavior.,

matters.headline: Your habits are not just choices.
matters.body: That may be why people in different circumstances face different hurdles. Success might depend more on the safety of your environment than on your internal strength.,

example.headline: A child in a quiet kitchen.
example.body: You watch a child sit alone. They look at a snack. They decide whether to eat it now or wait for a parent to return. The room is silent. You wonder if they are disciplined or just safe.,

question.headline: How much of your discipline is actually your own?

stat.label: the reduction in the correlation between waiting and achievement when controlling for background

claims.text: The marshmallow test is linked to problem behavior because it reflects aspects of a child's early environment rather than self-control.
claims.quote: These relationships were better explained by social support than by self-control, suggesting that the marshmallow test is predictive because it reflects aspects of a child's early environment that are important over the long term.

claims.text: When controlling for family background, early cognitive ability, and the home environment, the bivariate correlation between waiting an extra minute at age 4 and achievement at age 15 was reduced by two thirds.
claims.quote: But this bivariate correlation was only half the size of those reported in the original studies and was reduced by two thirds in the presence of controls for family background, early cognitive ability, and the home environment.

claims.text: Participants were less willing to wait for delayed rewards from less trustworthy characters, and perceived trustworthiness predicted willingness to delay gratification.
claims.quote: Across two experiments, participants were less willing to wait for delayed rewards from less trustworthy characters, and perceived trustworthiness predicted willingness to delay gratification.

claims.text: A board game designed to increase delay of gratification improved wait times during the Marshmallow Test in one study, but had no effect in a second study.
claims.quote: In Study 1, the intervention group also increased wait times during the Marshmallow Test versus controls (p=0. 047). In Study 2, there was no effect on Marshmallow Test wait times.

claims.text: Individuals who generally think and act in a future-oriented manner have a stronger ability to delay gratification.
claims.quote: Individuals who generally think and act in a future-oriented manner have a stronger ability to delay gratification.

verdict: The evidence shows that while the marshmallow test correlates with certain outcomes, these links are significantly weakened or explained away by family background and social factors.
caveat: The studies show mixed results regarding the effectiveness of specific interventions, such as board games, in actually improving delay of gratification.
caption:
The marshmallow test is often used to measure individual self-control. 

Research shows that this link is significantly weakened when you account for family background and social factors. Results on specific interventions like board games remain mixed. 

How much of your daily discipline is a result of your upbringing?
